name: Postural Restoration Institute (PRI)

lead: PRI is a posture method from physical therapist Ron Hruska built around breathing and body asymmetry.
The evidence base is thin, mostly case reports and basic physiology.

paras: Specific breathing and positioning exercises aim to reduce asymmetric patterns and reposition the ribcage and pelvis.
Not documented in the sources reviewed; delivered by licensed professionals.

lead: Postural Restoration is a posture-based approach to physical medicine developed by physical therapist Ron Hruska in the early 1990s. In 1999 he founded the Postural Restoration Institute in Lincoln, Nebraska, to train health professionals [1]. It uses manual and non-manual exercises to reposition and retrain the body toward neutral alignment [1].

Advocates claim it improves alignment, breathing mechanics and asymmetrical movement patterns. Wikipedia states there is little strong evidence that any specific posture leads to better medical outcomes [1].

paras: PRI targets asymmetrical patterned positions and aims to restore neutrality. Breathing is central, and advocates cite diaphragm function and the zone of apposition, where the diaphragm meets the rib cage [1].

No studies found. Wikipedia's references for the topic are described as a case report, an ethnography of the PRI community, a survey of physiotherapists' views on posture and older physiology papers on diaphragm mechanics [1].
